items.title: Manuel Joseph "Moose" Zanco Interview, 1959-11-25
items.q: they want to know, what is jazz supposed to be? Or what is Dixie Landon? Dixie Landon. Now, the way I look at it, it's each musician is playing a solo simultaneously.

ctx.x: I heard that Birmingham job, you couldn't remember anything about it, but from what I remember, that I was told, I think a girl who goes to school here, or had gone to school here, had a bunch over at Bruno's and she knows ice. And she had gotten her father to put up a pretty good bundle to bring the band up there for two hours and they followed a regular dance that they had at their house, didn't they?

Yeah, yeah. Yeah, that's right. Well, again too, now that goes back to the business angle, see, which I'm not too, too familiar with, but that's how we got to make the trip over there. Incidentally, we started playing, must have been, what time? 12, 12 o'clock, 3 o'clock, it was a ridiculous hour we started. But before this, they had a nice dance band there. I mean, these guys were strictly, you know, reading musicians that were very good. And one of the fellas, the guy who fronted his band was a trumpet man, and…
Well, do you think the guys listen to each other while they're playing?
